title: Wireless fully-implanted BCI power and data link
bottleneck: Cutting the cables means powering and reading an implant through skin and skull: inductive charging is inefficient and heats tissue, while wireless data links must push megabits through lossy tissue within milliwatt budgets. Batteries need replacement surgery; batteryless designs harvest too little power. Fully implanted, cable-free, high-bandwidth BCIs face coupled power-data-thermal constraints.
why_it_blocks: Tethered BCIs confine users to labs; true independence needs wireless implants. Until power and data cross the skin barrier efficiently, BCIs can't be everyday devices.
current_state: Percutaneous pedestals are being replaced by wireless prototypes in animals and early human work; fully implanted inductively charged systems are on translational paths. Human-grade wireless broadband implants are not yet demonstrated. Tissue attenuates radio signals unpredictably with posture and hydration, making wireless link budgets hard to guarantee.
